title: Food prices continue to rise. 8 money moves to cut costs at the grocery store
raw_text:

Prices are rising faster than they have in years — and that means your trips to the grocery store are getting more expensive. Luckily, we have some tips to help offset that premium.
The Consumer Price Index rose 0.5% month-over-month on a seasonally adjusted basis in May 2026, pushing the annual inflation rate to 4.2%, the first time it has been above the 4% mark in three years. This surge is mostly due to rising energy costs prompted by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East (energy prices rose 23.5% year-over-year).
To help you minimize rising costs as much as possible, CNBC Select has eight tips to save money on your next supermarket run.

Most grocery stores offer free loyalty programs. By signing up, you can benefit from member-only discounts that automatically deduct at checkout, without the need to clip coupons.
There are also premium memberships available that may help you save at certain stores if you're a frequent shopper.
For example, Walmart — one of the biggest grocery stores in the U.S. — offers Walmart+ for $98 per year (or $12.95 per month). This paid membership will earn you rewards on eligible purchase, which you can use toward a discount on your grocery bill.
You'll also get early access to deals, along with free pharmacy delivery, shipping, online pet care, flat tire repair and Paramount+ and Peacock subscriptions.
If you prefer to get your groceries delivered or shop at Whole Foods, Amazon offers Amazon Prime for $14.99 per month or $139 per year, which could help you save with exclusive deals and discounted same-day shipping on grocery purchases. You'll also get similar perks in-person and online at Whole Foods with this membership.
There's nothing like old-fashioned couponing and bargain hunting. These low-tech options are still a great way to save:
- Collect coupons: Look out for your favorite store's weekly circular in the mail, cut out any coupons that matter to you and save them for your next grocery run. If you prefer a more modern couponing experience, download your favorite grocery store's mobile app, browse available discounts and click to load coupons onto your digital loyalty card. Most of the time, the discounts will be applied automatically when you check out.
- Seek out sales: Keep an eye out for promotions that can help you save on everything from staples like milk and eggs to sweets like ice cream and cookies.
Wholesale clubs like Costco can help you rack up savings for buying in bulk. If you have a large family, joining a wholesale club can be a good idea. But remember that buying in bulk isn’t for everyone since you’ll have to spend more money upfront, even though you’re saving overall. This may not be an option depending on your cash flow.
Also, note that clubs come with membership fees. Currently, the cost of a Costco membership starts at $65 for Gold Star and doubles to $130 for Gold Star Executive. The cost can be worthwhile if you frequently stock up on items. Plus, you can optimize savings by using the Costco Anywhere Visa® Card by Citi (which has no annual fee, but requires an active Costco membership). (Read our review of the Costco Anywhere Visa Card.)

If you live near several grocery stores, compare prices and consider shopping at different stores for different products. Shopping around may not always be more affordable if you have to travel farther to other grocery stores, but it's worth considering.
If you currently shop at a high-end grocery store, consider switching to a store known for lower prices, like Walmart, Aldi or Trader Joe's.
While you're shopping at a particular grocery store, you can also shop by comparing unit prices. A unit price is the cost of an item per ounce, pound, quart or other unit of measure the item goes by. This lets you compare products to make sure you're getting the best value. You can calculate the unit price by dividing the total price of the item by the quantity (how much of the item there is). So, if a bag of 10 oranges costs $4.00, the unit price is $0.40 per orange.
Supermarkets are known to place costly, name-brand items at eye level, which can tempt you to spend more. But if you look at the top or bottom of the shelves, you’ll often find the best deals.
The generic brand version of a product at Walmart, Kroger, and Target could save shoppers up to 75% on some products, according to an April 2026 NetCredit study, which compared prices of brand-name versus store-name products across 171 grocery store items.
A gallon of generic milk, for example, could save shoppers 61% on average at these three stores compared to brand-name milk.

If you go to the supermarket without a list, it's easy to grab things you don’t need.
That's because your mind tends to switch between a deliberative state (where you're trying to make a decision) and an implementation state (where you're trying to take an action based on that decision), Annie Wilson, a senior lecturer of marketing at The Wharton School, told CNBC Select for a previous version of this article.
"So if you don't have a list, you're in that deliberative mindset and reacting to everything in the aisle you're in," she said. "That's why you end up purchasing things that are unplanned."
The next time you go to the grocery store, make sure you have a list and stick to it so you don’t end up overspending. You may also want to consider eating first to avoid a spur-of-the-moment item.
FAQs
Why are groceries so expensive?
Grocery prices have risen significantly since 2020 due to supply shortages and overall inflation. The consumer price index for May 2026 showed that inflation — including grocery inflation — was outpacing expectations.
What is the cheapest grocery store?
Does Medicare provide a grocery allowance?
Traditional Medicare does not offer a grocery allowance. However, some Medicare Advantage plans, like some Special Needs Plans (SNPs), do. Reach out to your provider to understand your benefits.
